subject: Pricing structure and seat-split recommendation for Clearline
messages:
From: Claire Moss <claire@clearline.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearline Procurement <procurement@clearline.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial quote — question about seat split and add-ons

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement flagged a couple of items we need clarified before we can move this to legal:

1) Can the 500-seat commitment be split across two tiers (200 Premium, 300 Standard) while keeping one billing contract? That affects pricing and how credits apply.
2) We use streaming inference heavily. Is there a way to bundle the streaming add-on as a discounted line item rather than per-token metering?
3) We have a one-time org change next quarter and may reallocate ~50 seats between teams — can we get a credit to move seats between tiers during the first 12 months?

Attached is a spreadsheet with our proposed seat split and current usage. Can you surface options that won’t force us into two separate contracts?

Regards,
Claire
Claire Moss
Head of Platform Ops, Clearline.ai
[Attachment: Clearline_Seat_Allocation_Request.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Claire Moss <claire@clearline.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial quote — question about seat split and add-ons

Hi Claire — thanks for the detail and spreadsheet. Quick answers up front, then I'll follow up with a short options table:

- Yes, a single contract can cover mixed tiers; we map seats to entitlement SKUs on our side and can produce a single invoice.
- Streaming can be packaged as a metered add-on with a blended rate for committed customers — we often offer a committed streaming block that behaves like a discounted line item.
- For one-time internal reallocation: we can do a one-time seat reclassification within the first 12 months with a small administrative fee or, alternatively, issue an equivalent credit if the net seat counts align.

I'll pull finance and discounts into thread to propose exact numbers.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing structure and seat-split recommendation for Clearline

Eve — forwarding Claire's ask and your note. A few constraints from my side:

- Discount tiers are tied to effective committed spend buckets. Splitting seats across tiers is fine but the aggregate committed spend needs to meet the discount threshold.
- For streaming, offering a committed block (e.g., 1B tokens/month) with a blended unit rate is doable, but we'd need to cap total overages or define a step-up price.
- Seat reclassification credit: finance prefers a credit approach (apply an account-level credit equal to expected difference) versus unlimited free swaps. We will need to quantify the administrative charge.

Proposed next step: Evelyn, can you send a short spreadsheet with two pricing scenarios: (A) single-contract with blended pricing and one-time 50-seat reclassification credit (amount), (B) two sub-licences under the same master contract (separate SKUs) with a smaller reclassification fee but clearer billing lines.

I can pre-approve up to a 10% discount on base list for this customer but anything beyond requires sales leadership sign-off.

-Jonas

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing structure and seat-split recommendation for Clearline

Adding finance perspective:

- If we do scenario A (blended), revenue recognition is straightforward but we should reserve a 5% margin buffer in the quote to protect against usage variance.
- Scenario B (separate SKUs) increases bookkeeping but provides clearer escalation paths for support tiers and SLA mapping — helpful for enterprise procurement teams.
- For the one-time reclassification: standard approach is credit = (delta in monthly price * remaining months) rounded to nearest $1k, with a $1,500 admin charge. For this deal size, that's acceptable.

Eve — if you share the customer spreadsheet with the seat counts and expected monthly streaming tokens, I’ll run quick pro forma numbers.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Manager, Revenue Ops

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Claire Moss <claire@clearl ine.ai>, Clearline Procurement <procurement@clearline.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing structure and seat-split recommendation for Clearline

Claire — following internal review, attached are two pricing scenarios (see summary below). Please let me know which you prefer and we'll lock the SOW/PO language accordingly.

Summary:
- Option A — Single contract, blended seat pricing
  - 500 seats (200 Premium, 300 Standard) under one contract, blended effective per-seat rate: $2.15 / seat / month (annualized).
  - Streaming committed block: 1B tokens/month at blended rate of $0.0014 / token (overage tiered).
  - One-time reclassification credit: we will offer a credit equal to the net difference for up to 50 seats once in the first 12 months, plus a $1,500 admin fee.

- Option B — Master contract with two SKUs (clear billing lines)
  - Premium SKU: $2.45 / seat / month (200 seats)
  - Standard SKU: $1.95 / seat / month (300 seats)
  - Streaming offered as a discounted add-on SKU; reclassification handled as above but invoiced per SKU.
  - If you choose B, we can reduce the admin fee to $750.

Next steps:
- Tell me preferred option and confirm streaming block size.
- If you want the reduced admin fee, we'll need a signed LOI committing to the 12-month term and the streaming committed block.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call later this week to walk pricing.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
